audit_rule: A later-commit message is a collision only when its complete text occurs case-insensitively, with runs of whitespace normalized and word boundaries around the message in the model context. A collision is GENERIC only when it has at most four whitespace-separated words, occurs as a whole phrase in ordinary prepared-repository text, contains none of the fixed defect/fix/test/error/security terms or issue/version/path/commit/code identifiers, and does not otherwise describe a defect, fix, or related issue. Ambiguous matches are INFORMATIVE. A case is retained only when all its matches are GENERIC; a case with no matches passes. Repeated identical messages are deduplicated per case while retaining the count and union of locations.

later_message_text_collisions.classification_reason: at most four words; occurs as a whole phrase in repository text; no defect/fix/test/error/security terms or technical identifiers

method: Audited every case ID in the supplied config. Built the same initial user message and system prompt as the benchmark, scanned all readable workspace files, and checked fixing-commit metadata, human scoring artifacts, model-visible Git history, safe tool names, and complete later-message strings. Applied the written audit rule uniformly; any informative or ambiguous match drops its case.
